summary: The signed-in preview opens a board by UUID and displays its ordered items read-only. Each selection or retry uses the existing SelectedRead handler, which resolves the session and checks current grants before reading items. Back to boards fetches a new list.
evidence: browser_opens_selected_board_by_id passed in headless Chromium. The initial list showed only 203 Quartz, 202 Review and 201 Review, with no item request. Clicking the last Review issued one selected GET for 201 and showed only 73 Sketch above 61 Ink. Back issued a list GET. Tab and Enter on the first Review issued one selected GET for 202 and showed only 62 Outline. Both destination responses were HTTP 200; neither view offered an editor.

browser_revoked_membership_blocks_selection passed. After the list mounted, an independent connection removed the Viewer's closed-workspace membership. Clicking the stale 201 button and then Retry destination each issued one GET for 201 and received HTTP 403. Both showed Destination unavailable without rows or sign-in. Back fetched No boards. After membership restoration, Refresh fetched only the list; clicking 201 again showed Sketch and Ink.

At the list, selection, denial and recovery checkpoints, fresh database connections confirmed the same sole session verifier and Viewer account, subscriptions to 201, 202 and 203, the expected membership, and unchanged ordered items on both Review boards, all at revision 1.

All four browser_preview cases passed serially, including the two inherited sign-in, list and logout cases. All eight loopback_board_access cases passed, including selected_board_read_checks_current_membership. The locked portable workspace suite passed all 23 tests; workspace formatting and git diff --check passed. The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs, so runner regressions remain for coordinator verification.

Selection, denial and explicit recovery matched the synthetic reference outcomes recorded in the roadmap. Destination-specific service failure, missing-board and expired-session screens were not separately exercised in Chromium. In-page return does not establish URL/history, full grid/sidebar, saved views, paging or live revocation parity. Only isolated headless profiles were run.
